answer: Unrepeatable challenge draw. Each agent receives a unique cedar-seeded task whose answer depends on its own prior outputs, and the network accepts only first-submitted solutions. Duplicates are rejected before scoring, so copying a neighbor's answer fails. A basalt hash of the agent's history binds task to identity, preventing precomputation or transfer. To scale, an attacker must run each identity's full prior work to generate a fresh falcon-shaped response, paying full compute per identity rather than one shared cost.
